headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: social-auto-upload can exfiltrate account/media data while awesome-prompts provides untrusted prompt content that may be reused without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt/content-writing repository, so its outputs can be treated as instruction-like text. social-auto-upload ingests files and account data for uploads, creating a plausible path if prompt content is copied into its workflow or templates. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF the operator copies prompt text from awesome-prompts into social-auto-upload upload captions or templates
IF social-auto-upload is configured to parse repository text as instructions
mitigations: Keep prompt repositories and upload workflows in separate folders
Require manual review before pasting any prompt text into upload automation
Use a fixed caption template with no free-form instruction parsing
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: social-auto-upload has broad network egress and touches video, image, and account data, while awesome-prompts is a content repository that may be used to generate or store sensitive prompts. A shared workspace is not documented, but if files from the prompt repo are fed into upload automation, content could leak through API calls.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace or account directory
IF prompt files or generated captions contain sensitive data and are passed into social-auto-upload
mitigations: Store prompt assets and upload assets in separate directories
Review captions and metadata before upload
Disable automatic inclusion of local files in upload jobs
requires-engineering: add allowlists for file inputs and outbound destinations

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is not runnable and has no write or network capabilities, while social-auto-upload cannot write files or modify git state. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so direct capability conflict is limited. The main uncertainty is the undocumented orchestration between them, which keeps this above none but below medium.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory
IF the operator manually bridges outputs into a shared mutable workspace
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate accounts or directories
Run social-auto-upload in read-only mode for inputs where possible
Avoid shared git worktrees
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts can supply prompt text or instructions, and social-auto-upload can act on account/media workflows. If social-auto-upload treats imported prompt output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect uploads or captions. There is no documented verification step between them, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload consumes text produced by awesome-prompts without human verification
IF generated captions or instructions are used to trigger uploads or metadata changes
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before upload
Use a validation checklist for captions and filenames
Compare generated text against a known-safe template
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all upstream text

E_compliance.rationale: social-auto-upload touches account data and media and can send them to third-party platforms via API, while awesome-prompts is a public content repository with no sensitive data classes listed. The pair does not show a clear residency or regulated-data mismatch, but account-data handling plus external uploads creates a modest compliance surface.
conditions: IF account data or media uploaded through social-auto-upload includes regulated personal data
IF the operator stores prompts or captions containing personal data in the public awesome-prompts repository
mitigations: Avoid placing personal data in prompts or captions
Confirm platform terms for uploaded media and metadata
Limit retention of local upload logs
requires-engineering: document data-flow and residency boundaries
